stem: A price index uses base-year prices as weights. Which of the following named index does this describe?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Paasche uses current-year quantities as weights, not base-year prices as weights.
Laspeyres Price Index weights prices by base-year quantities: P_L = (sum p1*q0) / (sum p0*q0) * 100.
Fisher is the geometric mean of Laspeyres and Paasche; it does not use base-year weights exclusively.
Marshall-Edgeworth uses the average of base-year and current-year quantities as weights.

explanation: The Laspeyres Price Index is defined as the ratio of current-year prices to base-year prices, weighted by base-year quantities: P_L = (sum p1*q0) / (sum p0*q0) * 100. Using base-year weights is the defining characteristic that distinguishes it from Paasche (current-year weights) and other indices.

explanation_sections.punchline: Base-year quantity weights identify the Laspeyres index uniquely; Paasche uses current-year quantity weights.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the method: recall which named index uses which set of weights. Laspeyres = base-year (q0) weights; Paasche = current-year (q1) weights; Fisher = geometric mean of both; Marshall-Edgeworth = average of q0 and q1.
explanation_sections.lesson: Laspeyres anchors on the past (base year); Paasche anchors on the present (current year). Memorise the anchor, not the formula.
explanation_sections.timing: About 30-40 seconds. Pure recall; no computation needed. The trap is confusing Laspeyres with Paasche.
